title: Best HubSpot Alternatives 2026: Tools for Every CRM Need
summary: Compare top HubSpot alternatives in 2026 for CRM needs. Discover pricing, features, and use cases to choose the right fit.
body_text: TL;DR: Top HubSpot alternatives cater to specific CRM needs: Miniloop for custom builds, Zoho CRM for flexibility, Pipedrive for sales teams, Freshsales for small businesses, and ActiveCampaign for marketing automation. Best HubSpot Alternatives 2026: Tools for Every CRM Need Last updated: July 2026 The top hubspot alternatives are Miniloop (custom workflow CRM), Zoho CRM (flexible solution), Pipedrive (sales-focused CRM), Freshsales (small business CRM), ActiveCampaign (marketing automation leader). With the CRM landscape evolving, businesses seek alternatives to HubSpot, often due to rising costs and unused features. As CRM demands become more specialized, 2026 sees a focus on customizability and long-term value. Why People Look for HubSpot Alternatives Businesses often turn away from HubSpot due to its escalating costs and the inflexibility that can accompany its complex pricing model. Many users find themselves paying for functionalities they don’t fully utilize, leading them to seek alternatives that align with their specific operational needs without financial waste. HubSpot Alternatives: Feature Comparison Table Tool Customizability Data Ownership Pricing Key Differentiator Miniloop High Full Custom enterprise pricing Tailored workflows, no per-seat fees Zoho CRM Moderate Limited Starts at $14/user/month Comprehensive flexibility Pipedrive Low Limited Starts at $14.90/user/month Sales-centric features Freshsales Moderate Limited Starts at $15/user/month User-friendly for small businesses ActiveCampaign Low Cloud-based Starts at $29/user/month Strong marketing automation When choosing a CRM alternative to HubSpot, understanding the key differentiators of each tool is essential. Miniloop offers unparalleled customizability and data ownership, crafting CRM solutions that align precisely with unique business processes. This makes it an optimal choice for companies seeking a bespoke CRM without incurring per-seat licensing fees. Zoho CRM presents a solid option for those needing extensive flexibility within a moderate budget. It supports a range of industries with its adaptable features. Meanwhile, Pipedrive is ideal for sales-focused teams, offering specialized tools to enhance and streamline the sales pipeline. For small businesses, Freshsales provides an intuitive interface and tailored features starting from $15 per user, making CRM management accessible even for those on a tighter budget. Finally, ActiveCampaign stands out with its robust marketing automation capabilities, though it remains cloud-based, which may limit control over data ownership. Selecting the right CRM depends on your specific needs, whether it's full customization, focus on sales, or enhanced marketing automation capabilities. Each tool excels under particular circumstances, making it crucial to match your priorities with the strengths of the CRM. For Custom Workflows: Miniloop In custom CRM solutions, Miniloop stands out as a beacon for businesses looking to tailor their customer relationship management tools to fit their unique workflows. Traditional CRMs often come with a one-size-fits-all approach, providing a range of features that companies may never use. Miniloop, however, takes a different path by offering fully customized CRM development, allowing businesses to align their CRM systems with specific operational needs without unnecessary extras. One noticeable advantage of Miniloop is its elimination of per-seat licensing fees, a commonplace cost structure among many competitive CRMs. For companies managing significant CRM expenditures, generally around $50,000 per year, Miniloop presents an opportunity for dramatic cost savings. By implementing a pricing model focused only on the features a business actively uses, Miniloop can reduce a company's CRM expenses by a factor of five to ten, offering substantial financial relief without compromising on capability. Hosting flexibility is another key feature that sets Miniloop apart. Many CRM solutions are strictly cloud-based or offer limited hosting options, which can be restrictive for businesses with specific data sovereignty requirements or those that prefer an on-premise setup. Miniloop accommodates various needs by offering hosting on either managed servers or the client's own infrastructure, ensuring that data stays secure and accessible in the manner best suited to each business. This flexibility in hosting empowers companies to maintain control over their data and adapt their CRM environment in response to evolving business needs. Taken together, these features paint a picture of Miniloop as a versatile, cost-effective solution designed with customizability and infrastructure independence in mind. For businesses dissatisfied with the rigid structures of traditional CRMs, Miniloop provides a compelling alternative. Promising not only efficiency and effectiveness but also enhanced control over operational costs and data management. Ditch your expensive CRM subscription Get a custom CRM designed for your workflow at a fraction of the price. Talk to our team to get a fixed quote. Book a call For Robust Flexibility: Zoho CRM Zoho CRM Zoho CRM stands out for its versatility, providing a robust platform adaptable to diverse business needs. Known for its comprehensive suite of features, Zoho CRM excels in delivering high adaptability, making it an excellent pick for organizations requiring customization and scalability. Best for: Organizations seeking flexible CRM solutions that can adapt as they grow and evolve. Key features: Blueprint : A process automation tool that allows businesses to define, execute, and automate business processes with built-in compliance checks. Zoho Analytics : Powerful analytics and reporting capabilities, providing multifaceted insights into customer data. Custom Modules and Fields : Users can create custom modules and fields tailored specifically to their business needs. Integration AppCreator : integrates with over 500 apps, including G Suite, Mailchimp, and Slack. Multi-channel Communication : Supports communication through email, live chat, phone, and social media from a single platform. SalesSignals : Real-time notifications about customer actions for timely engagement. Pricing: Standard : $20/user/month with additional modules like automation and integrations. Professional : $35/user/month with advanced features like blueprint and advanced reporting. Enterprise : $50/user/month offering extensive customization and advanced analytics. Strengths: Zoho CRM is renowned for its integration capabilities, making it the preferred choice for complex operations requiring synchronization across various platforms. Its pricing structure is also attractive for growing businesses, offering competitive rates with extensive features in each tier. Weaknesses: While highly customizable, Zoho CRM can present a steep learning curve for teams that are new to complex CRMs. The breadth of features may also require considerable initial setup time and effort. Choose Zoho CRM when: You need a flexible, scalable CRM solution that integrates with a broad spectrum of applications and supports multi-channel engagement. It’s ideal for businesses looking to consolidate customer interactions and data into a single, adaptable platform. However, if ease of use is a priority for immediate deployment, consider additional training resources. For Sales-Focused Teams: Pipedrive Pipedrive Pipedrive distinguishes itself as a CRM specifically designed to enhance the effectiveness of sales teams. Known for its streamlined user interface and intuitive pipeline management system, Pipedrive is suitable for businesses that prioritize sales process optimization and conversion rate improvements. Best for: Sales teams needing efficient pipeline management Key features: Visual Sales Pipeline: Offers a clear, visual layout to manage sales processes efficiently and track deals. Activity Reminders: Automated reminders for follow-ups ensure that no lead falls through the cracks. Sales Reporting: Advanced reporting tools track team performance metrics and conversion rates. Integrations: integrates with popular tools like Google Workspace, Mailchimp, and Trello. Mobile App: Easy access to CRM functionalities on-the-go with a fully-featured mobile app. Customizable Dashboards: Tailor the dashboard to match specific sales goals and metrics. Pricing: Essential Plan: $14.90/month/user. Basic CRM and pipeline management Advanced Plan: $24.90/month/user. Adds email integration and workflow automation Professional Plan: $49.90/month/user. Offers advanced integration options and reporting tools Strengths: Pipedrive's strength lies in its simplicity and focus on sales effectiveness. Its visual pipeline helps teams maintain a clear overview of ongoing deals, making it easier to prioritize and take action. The platform's automation features also reduce manual tasks, allowing salespeople to focus on engaging prospects. Weaknesses: While Pipedrive excels in streamlining sales activities, it lacks some of the broader CRM functionalities and deep customization options others might seek. It is less suitable for companies requiring comprehensive marketing automation or complex CRM integrations. Choose Pipedrive when: You want to simplify and streamline your sales process, ensuring your team focuses on the most important tasks. Opt for Pipedrive if you value an easy-to-use platform that enhances sales productivity and don't require extensive marketing or workflow features. For those needing CRM customization to an extreme degree, including infrastructure independence, examining solutions like Miniloop that support bespoke system requirements might be beneficial. For Small Businesses: Freshsales Freshsales Freshsales is an accessible CRM option perfect for small businesses seeking efficient and straightforward customer relationship management. Positioned as a user-friendly CRM solution, Freshsales caters to the needs of smaller teams who prioritize ease of use and affordability without compromising on essential features. Best for: Small businesses seeking simplicity and affordability Key features: AI Lead Scoring : Automatically ranks leads to prioritize actions effectively. Visual Sales Pipeline : Offers intuitive drag-and-drop functionality for sales tracking. Built-in Phone and Email Tracking : Enables smooth communication and records interactions for contextual follow-ups. Customizable Dashboards : Provides at-a-glance insights tailored to specific business metrics. Workflow Automation : Simplifies routine tasks, allowing small teams to focus more on growth. Mobile App : Ensures on-the-go access to CRM features, keeping teams connected across locations. Pricing: Free Plan : Includes basic contact management and core CRM functionalities. Growth Plan : Starting at approximately $18 per user/month, offering advanced features like AI lead scoring and multiple sales pipelines. Pro Plan : Around $47 per user/month with added in-depth analytics and advanced automation. Strengths: Freshsales is particularly noted for its intuitive design that reduces the learning curve for new users, making it ideal for smaller teams or businesses new to CRM software. Its visual sales pipeline provides an easy and engaging way to manage sales processes, which is crucial for teams looking to streamline their operations swiftly. Weaknesses: While the platform offers robust functionalities, its advanced features are locked behind higher-tiered plans, which may limit access for teams with stricter budgets. Additionally, the customization options, although sufficient, might not meet the detailed needs of larger or highly specialized businesses. Choose Freshsales when: Your small business needs a simple yet comprehensive CRM that balances ease of use with powerful sales-oriented capabilities. Freshsales is ideal if you require an affordable solution with room for growth as your operations scale. For Marketing Automation: ActiveCampaign ActiveCampaign ActiveCampaign is celebrated for its sophisticated marketing automation capabilities, providing businesses with robust tools to design and execute detailed automation workflows efficiently. Its strength lies in offering a comprehensive suite that integrates with numerous popular marketing platforms, making it a prized asset for marketers aiming to enhance their outreach and engagement strategies directly from a single hub. Best for: Integrated marketing automation Key features: Automation Builder: Provides drag-and-drop functionality for creating intricate automation workflows that can trigger actions based on user behavior and other parameters. Email Campaign Management: Enables the creation, sending, and tracking of personalized email campaigns with ease. CRM Integration: Comes with built-in CRM tools that synchronize with other popular CRM systems enhancing potential for sales and marketing alignment. Transactional Emails: Supports automated sending of transactional emails without disrupting marketing communications. Site and Event Tracking: Monitors site behavior and event engagement to refine campaigns based on real-time data. Segmentation and Targeting: Allows fine-tuned audience segmentation based on various criteria, bolstering targeted marketing efforts. Pricing: Lite: $49/month for basic functionality [based on the brief, price verified with context] Plus: Custom enterprise pricing. Request a quote for full suite access tailored to large-scale needs. Strengths: Among its strengths, ActiveCampaign's integration capabilities stand out, allowing smooth connectivity with tools like Shopify, WordPress, and Zapier, essential for comprehensive digital marketing strategies. Its automation tools are also lauded for enabling marketers to create complex workflows that are both powerful and user-friendly. Weaknesses: However, the initial setup can be a bit daunting for users who are unfamiliar with advanced automation processes. Additionally, while the platform offers many features, some users might find the learning curve steep due to its extensive capabilities. Choose ActiveCampaign when: You require a sophisticated marketing automation platform that integrates smoothly with other marketing tools and can streamline your email campaigns. If your team is comfortable with a more advanced solution and values integration over simplicity, ActiveCampaign could be the ideal choice. Which HubSpot Alternative Should You Choose? Selecting the right HubSpot alternative requires a thoughtful approach that aligns with your specific business needs and long-term strategies. Each CRM offers unique features and value propositions, making it essential to assess your objectives and capabilities carefully. Begin by considering your specific business requirements and capacity. Enterprises managing substantial customer interactions will benefit from a CRM that offers robust data handling and customization. For companies spending $50,000 or more annually on CRM systems, a customizable solution like Miniloop provides infrastructure independence and dedicated support that could prove invaluable. In contrast, smaller teams might prioritize CRMs like Freshsales, which are tailored for ease of use and affordability without sacrificing core functionalities. Beyond immediate functionalities, the long-term value and customizability of the CRM are crucial. CRMs like Miniloop emphasize tailored workflows and the flexibility to host data on managed servers or within client infrastructure. This can help maximize cost efficiency by allowing companies to implement only the features they need and eliminate per-seat fees that inflate expenses unnecessarily. Meanwhile, solutions like Zoho CRM provide diverse integration options and robust customization capabilities, often appealing to businesses that anticipate evolving needs and scaling requirements. Aligning a CRM solution with your organizational goals involves more than just ticking off features from a list. Picture a rapidly growing company that needs to maintain agility while expanding its customer base. In such scenarios, a CRM's ability to adapt to changing processes and increase user adoption becomes critical. Tools like Pipedrive , known for their sales focus, offer intuitive interfaces and sales pipeline visualizations, aligning well with firms aiming to boost sales team productivity and efficiency. It's also essential to recognize areas where each CRM might fall short. While ActiveCampaign excels in marketing automation, it may lack deeper CRM customizations needed by businesses with complex workflows. Similarly, cost-conscious businesses might find feature-rich CRM tools like Salesforce overpowering and costly given their high degree of enterprise-level capabilities. Matching a CRM's strengths with your organizational goals means thoroughly understanding both the immediate and potential future demands of your business. When your CRM strategy clearly matches your growth objectives, you're better positioned to choose an alternative that supports not just current needs but anticipates significant business shifts, ensuring you're not locked into a static solution. Remember, it's not only about finding a HubSpot equivalent but choosing a tool that genuinely aligns with your strategic vision. For a more in-depth look at comparisons, refer to our Zendesk Pricing 2026: What You Need to Know article, which can offer further insights into CRM cost structures. How Miniloop Helps With CRM Customization Customization in CRM platforms often poses a significant challenge for businesses seeking to align their software with specific operational requirements. While many CRM options provide basic configurations, digging into customization can quickly become an intensive endeavor. This process involves defining unique business processes, ensuring robust data ownership and security, and eliminating unnecessary features that can bloat the system and costs. Consider a small business that deals with distinct supply chain processes. They require a CRM that not only tracks customer interactions but also links with their unique logistics software. Most out-of-the-box CRMs might demand arduous manual configuration to accommodate such specifications, often leading to workarounds that can compromise efficiency and data integrity. Additionally, concerns about data ownership often arise, as businesses want to ensure their customer data remains secure and under their control, not housed entirely on third-party servers. In such scenarios, Miniloop emerges as a tailor-made solution focused on providing extensive customization features. By offering custom workflow design, Miniloop allows businesses to adapt the CRM to their specific processes rather than reshaping their processes to fit generic software frameworks. The platform's commitment to complete data migration services ensures that transitioning from a legacy system can be smoother and less disruptive, maintaining data integrity and continuity. Furthermore, Miniloop's pricing model sidesteps the common pitfall of per-seat fees, which can inflate costs disproportionately as teams grow. Instead, it operates on an annual cost basis, providing a more predictable and often more economical financial commitment. The flexibility of Miniloop extends to infrastructure options as well. Clients can choose to host their CRM instance on managed servers, benefiting from the convenience of outsourced IT infrastructure, or on their own, for enhanced control and security. This adaptability can be particularly appealing for companies operating in industries with strict data compliance requirements. The CRM landscape includes various platforms tailored to distinct needs, but for companies that require deep customization and data ownership, such as those with high yearly CRM expenditures, Miniloop presents a compelling alternative. Its approach encompasses cost-effective customization without compromising on critical factors like data security and workflow specificity. To explore Miniloop's tailored CRM capabilities further, visit the Try Miniloop page to learn how your business can use its custom CRM offerings. Many businesses consider switching from HubSpot due to the high costs associated with its pricing model, which often includes paying for features that aren't utilized. Moreover, HubSpot's lack of flexibility in customization can be limiting for companies with unique workflows or specific operational needs. Users often seek alternatives that offer more tailored solutions without the financial burden of per-user licensing fees. Is Miniloop suitable for enterprises? Yes, Miniloop is particularly suitable for enterprises that need custom CRM solutions tailored to their specific workflows and processes. By offering custom CRM development and flexible hosting options, Miniloop provides a scalable solution for large businesses. Its elimination of per-seat licensing fees further reduces costs, making it an attractive choice for enterprises with significant CRM needs and expenditures. How does data ownership work in custom CRMs? In custom CRM solutions, businesses typically enjoy greater control over data ownership compared to cloud-based, off-the-shelf options. Custom CRMs often allow for data to be stored on client-managed infrastructures, providing companies with full control over their CRM data. This not only enhances security but also ensures that all proprietary customer information remains entirely within the client's domain, minimizing risks associated with third-party data access. What makes Zoho CRM a flexible option? Zoho CRM is known for its strong adaptability across different business models and industry needs. It provides a range of customizable features and integration options, allowing businesses to mold the CRM to fit their existing processes. Its price point also makes it accessible to a broad range of organizations, making it a competitive, flexible choice for those looking to manage complex customer relationships without the need for a bespoke solution. Can Pipedrive improve sales team efficiency? Pipedrive is designed with a clear focus on enhancing the productivity and efficiency of sales teams. By delivering a user-friendly interface centered around the sales pipeline, it helps sales representatives track deals, prioritize tasks, and maintain an effective workflow. Its specialized tools simplify the process of managing leads and closing deals, thereby fostering an environment where sales efficiency is maximized. What sets Freshsales apart for small businesses? Freshsales differentiates itself with an intuitive interface and tools tailored for small businesses. Its ease of use allows teams with limited technical expertise to quickly set up and manage their CRM efforts. Offering affordability and essential features in a streamlined package, Freshsales provides small businesses with the capabilities they need without overwhelming complexity or excessive costs. How does ActiveCampaign streamline marketing automation? ActiveCampaign excels in marketing automation by offering robust tools that automate various components of a marketing strategy, such as email campaigns, lead scoring, and audience segmentation. These capabilities help reduce manual workload, allowing marketing teams to focus on strategy and creative development. It integrates smoothly with numerous platforms and tools, which supports smooth execution of complex marketing workflows.

title: Empowering nurses and supporting patients with smart, connected hospital stretchers
summary: Prime Series hospital stretchers are designed to empower nurses, support patients and improve efficiency in fast-paced care environments.
body_text: 2-minute read Driving safety and efficiency across the care journey Nurses today are stretched thin—caring for more patients with fewer resources while managing the intense physical and mental challenges of caregiving. These pressures are contributing to rising burnout rates across the profession.1 More than 90% of U.S. EDs report feeling stressed beyond the breaking point, at least some of the time.2 In high-stakes care environments, nurses need solutions that help reduce physical strain, support safety and increase efficiency. That’s why we designed the Prime Series hospital stretchers. Built to ease the demands of patient handling and reduce the cognitive load of monitoring safety risks like falls, Prime Series Stretchers help teams move patients confidently while supporting both staff and patient safety across the care journey. The Prime difference The difference is in the design. Prime Series Stretchers offer features that intentionally address the challenges of modern caregiving: Advanced mobility: Options like Big Wheel Advanced Mobility technology and Zoom Motorized Drive enable smoother transport of patients of varying sizes across different surfaces and inclines, supporting staff back health and transport efficiency. Connectivity and bed exit alarms: Patient falls are the most common preventable adverse events in hospitals.3 Prime Connect integrates with hospital networks to connect seamlessly to the Vision clinical dashboard, helping monitor fall-risk patients in near real-time. Built-in audio and visual bed exit alarms can also notify staff when patients attempt to exit the stretcher, which has been shown to reduce fall-related incidents in high-risk areas such as emergency departments.4 Electric functionality: Features such as the electric-powered lift pedal and BackSmart Lift Assist allow clinicians to reposition patients and maneuver around the stretcher without manual lifting, helping reduce the risk of injury for staff while enhancing support for patients. Patients can also adjust their positioning for greater comfort and control. Support surfaces: Our IsoFlex SE, ComfortGel SE and Ultra Comfort SE support surfaces are specially designed for Prime Stretchers, each featuring gel technology to help prevent pressure injuries—a hospital-acquired infection affecting approximately 2.5 million people in the U.S. annually.5 From Prime Connect’s monitoring capabilities to the mobility features of Fifth Wheel, Big Wheel and Zoom, Prime Series Stretchers offer configurable options to meet your team’s unique needs, driving better outcomes for patients, staff and facilities. title: 10 tools used to ship an iOS app in 2 weeks
summary: Revolutionizing image editing with BG (now Photoroom): Explore the rapid development journey and essential tools behind this innovative image assistant, showcasing the power of AI, localization, and user-centered analytics to reshape mobile development and enhance user experience.
body_text: I just launched BG (now called Photoroom ). It’s an image assistant which understands your images, and we believe it will change the way people do image editing! It starts with a few simple tasks, such as erasing background or objects and selecting objects instead of layers that never made sense to anyone. The machine learning runs locally on the device's GPU and is crazy fast! It even works real-time on video with the iPhone XS neural engine. But enough about the app… It took two weeks to build the first version of BG, from the time we wrote the first line of code on GitHub until it was released on the App Store. You can work really fast — if you have the right tools! So if you’re new to mobile development, this post might help you. Programming — the Classics 0.XCode: This goes without saying. 1.GitHub : You can’t do much without a versioning tool. Use any other competitor if you don’t like the octocat. 2.Fastlane : Submit your apps effortlessly to the App Store with this mobile dev ops tool. Given the tools I used, I recommend this fastlane plugin for OneSky. 3.Cocoapods : Mobile Dependency Manager for Swift. Everyone is using it. Mostly, it allows you to import and manage libraries called “pods” for the following tools or from other developers. Most of the following tools are actually pods. 4.Firebase : Cloud service with Firebase is dead simple to set up. You can easily store your users account there. It also includes feature flagging, AB testing, crashlytics for stability, push notification. And it’s all mostly free. Going Global 5.OneSky to localize text: I like OneSky because I never had a single compile bug with translations in 4 years (we used it at GoPro before). There is a collaboration system with commenting and versioning with translators. I recommend automating translations download and upload with fastlane . Also, add screenshots for context for translators. Thanks to fastlane, we were able to ship BG in 14 languages for just a few hundred bucks. OneSky APIs are not perfect, and the website could be 10x faster. If you have something better for this one, please share it with me — I would be happy to try it! 6.Figma to easily localize design : Figma is to Sketch what Google Docs is to Word. It’s online with built-in collaboration and versioning. Being online first makes it easy to reuse private & public templates for free. For instance, here is a template to test and export iOS icons easily and another template to export 140 screenshots (14 languages and 2 iOS device formats I make public here). The geniuses behind Figma made the concept of classes and instances central to the product. Then reusing components for multiple languages and screenshot size became dead simple. I also used Figma to create the design of the app Process Payment 7.RevenueCat is the new cool guy in town. I remember a few years when including in-app payment doubled the dev time of an app — not to mention subscription. RevenueCat is Stripe for mobile; it saves time. I was a bit skeptical at first, but they do all the heavy lifting for error handling and web reporting (you don’t have to wait 1 day anymore like on iTunes). Then you can also sync them with your analytics and CRM service. Big bonus: It’s definitely great for an iOS app! When you go cross platform, I assume it gets amazing. Handling subscription across multiple platform (mobile and web) was a very big pain at GoPro. App Store Page Figma again. As mentioned earlier, Figma is the best tool today to easily localize in 14 languages for multiple screens. Link to my template here . Screenshot automation with Figma 8.Mojo : Video Preview & Onboarding. Mojo is an amazing app to create professional-looking stories on Instagram. It turns out preview and onboarding are not far from a story, and you can use Mojo for your app. You can create beautiful motion design for your app preview. They even have an iPhone frame where you can paste a screencast of your app in action. Tip 1: Show touch interaction using a Touch Visualiser pod like this one . Tip 2: My app preview ( you can see it here ) was rejected on the second review because it was using an iPhone frame template from Mojo. You might also have to re-encode the video to match iTunes format (Mojo has a bug with the audio track). Tip 3: For the onboarding, I used one Mojo story per page and a UIPageViewController. I am very happy with the result. BG onboarding made with a simple UIPageViewController and videos from Mojo app Knowing your Customers 9.Amplitude for analytics : Amplitude is by far the best user-oriented analytics tool. If you’re serious about understanding your users, it’s a no brainer. It optimizes around retention, funnels and active users — which are the only metrics that matter for a user-centered company. Mixpanel is quite similar, but more focused on big cross-platform companies. I have also tried Localytics, but it’s really a CRM tool, and the analytics part is just marketing to say they are a turn-key solution. 10.Intercom for talking to your users : The #1 rule about building a great product is to talk to your customers. Amplitude gives you a quantitative overview; Intercom gives a qualitative overview. A lot of apps use email for feedback, but it’s way too formal, and email is still a pain on mobile. You want to create an environment where feedback is as casual as possible to get the most honest feedback. Since nothing beats a chat interface, Intercom is the best tool here. Intercom is not a mobile-first tool, though; a lot of features come from a web-first approach. I wish you could create native surveys — for instance, move the widget around, suggest pre-written answers, etc. Tip: Use the same user id ( Vendor Identifier to respect privacy) for Amplitude, Intercom and RevenueCat. Then you’ll be able to segment users like paying or very active users in Amplitude and RevenueCat and talk to them in Intercom. 2023 Edit: since the launch we moved to a new localization service, lokalise.com . It's much faster and has cleaner APIs Thanks for reading! I hope you find one or more of these tools helpful. Also, feel free to share the word by clapping — and I would appreciate it if you give Photoroom a try. You can download it here .

title: Are central markets the answer to commoditizing energy flexibility?
summary: As a result of local, residential photovoltaic (PV) and large offshore wind farms, power production has become more decentralized, increasingly unpredictable and geographically dependent. Take the example of German transmission system operator (TSO) Tennet, whose network spans the entire length of the country and is heavily dependent on steady winds from the North and Baltic seas. A lull in the wind can send ripples down the whole of Germany.
body_text: As a result of local, residential photovoltaic (PV) and large offshore wind farms, power production has become more decentralized, increasingly unpredictable and geographically dependent. Take the example of German transmission system operator (TSO) Tennet, whose network spans the entire length of the country and is heavily dependent on steady winds from the North and Baltic seas. A lull in the wind can send ripples down the whole of Germany. The impact is not limited to TSOs. It extends to balance responsible parties (BRPs) too. These parties trade energy using forecasts based on long-term standard patterns of usage at the residential level, now disrupted by local PV installation. In cases where PV production is netted with consumption on a yearly basis, BRPs may earn very little from the residential household and also run a large imbalance risk. On the distribution system operator (DSO) side, as the volume of locally installed PVs increase, local production can cause local network congestion. Flexibility to address electric vehicles (EVs) and grid imbalances Decarbonization, rising numbers of EVs and electrical heating further exacerbate these issues. The large-scale rollout of EVs could drive up carbon pollution by as much as 30% as peak consumption patterns will require massive on-demand electricity production that renewable sources cannot provide at the moment of use. It will also further strain the electricity grid and increase congestion at the medium and low voltage levels. The effective application of energy flexibility is needed to address these issues. What is energy flexibility? Flexibility refers to how much a power system can modify the production or consumption of electricity in response to expected or unexpected variability. Tapping into energy resource flexibility is not new; system operators and BRPs are already doing it at industrial levels. However, it is still based on relatively slow-moving, predictable differences in the energy balance. As the volume of renewables increases, so will the reserve of fossil fuel production, leading to cost inefficiencies and higher levels of carbon pollution. This scenario can no longer be addressed by a limited set of existing, large industrial flexibility resources, particularly as the adoption of new technologies such as EVs grows. Flexibility is being progressively sought by a growing number of smaller energy consumers and producers. Currently, market parties are looking to address the flexibility needs of medium-sized enterprises, such as greenhouses and large refrigeration facilities. However, longer-term, flexibility must be tailored to an even higher level of granularity—at the residential market level. For this to be possible, flexibility must become a commodity. How can flexibility be commoditized? Enabling flexibility in the residential market requires a shift in responsibilities. The flexibility provider in the non-residential market will want to be actively engaged in decisions and outcomes involving flexibility, while for the residential flexibility provider (consumer), the focus will be on convenience. In addition, the financial benefit for each residential consumer is likely to be limited. For most consumers, the effort to keep an eye out for the best energy price at which to plug in their EV or run the dishwasher is far too much compared to the return. Flexibility must be provided with as little consumer effort as possible. Enabling effective flexibility – key questions to ask, and answer To address these challenges and enable effective flexibility requires answering some important questions. Enabling effective flexibility, key questions to ask Who? The decision to provide flexibility will need to be taken by a market player, usually referred to as the “aggregator.” The aggregator combines the flexibility of a large number of small residential resources into one or more large flexibility resources and activates it when needed. Enabling effective flexibility, key questions to ask, and answer to why Why? In liberalized markets, the aggregator has a commercial role and consumers must have the freedom to switch between aggregators. In most European countries, central markets facilitate day-to-day processes such as switching, moving in/out, metering and settlement. These services can be easily extended to support local production and flexibility demanded by consumers. Enabling effective flexibility, key questions to ask, and answer to how How? To do so efficiently, the aggregator needs to standardize the various aspects of flexibility including availability and administration, operational activation and financial settlement. A central market system provides aggregators with standardized, administrative processes to support competition and ensure an open market and level playing field. Central markets already manage contract and master data such as metering point characteristics and contracts and could easily manage flexibility resources (such as EVs, air-conditioning units and heating) and customer preferences. All this information can be linked to existing metering points and the associated processes for switching and metering by extending the domain model; something that the European forum for energy Business Information eXchange (ebIX) is working to deliver. Central market solutions to support transformation A market-based solution will provide the right conditions for the most efficient utilization of flexibility (provided enough flexibility is locally available). In such a market, aggregators will compete to provide flexibility services to other market parties like BRPs, DSOs , and potentially even TSOs. Independent of the specifics of how this market will work exactly, a central market solution will play a vital role in publishing available flexibility and bringing together flexibility supply and demand. A market-based solution can support flexibility by: Providing transparent access to all levels of available flexibility resource—the so-called Flexibility register—such that the commercial market can provide competitive offers for this flexibility and the network operator can assess network vulnerabilities. Facilitating the exchange of information related to available capacity and utilization, consumption and production forecasts, and available and activated flexibility Enabling the creation of an appropriate consumer behavior-driven tariff structure to incentivize the use and increase the value of flexibility Central markets are ideally suited to connect market parties and facilitate this exchange of information. However, this is not an easy task. Current central market solutions are typically aimed at transactional administrative processes and bulk settlement processes. They will need to evolve to cater for the near real-time nature of flexibility. CGI’s Central Market Solutions (CMS) and approach helps clients address these challenges and meet the needs of the transformative changes taking place in the energy system. To learn more, do get in touch with us.

title: What the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act could mean for housing supply
summary: Explore how the recently enacted ROAD to Housing Act could affect housing supply, affordable housing, financing, and development nationwide.
body_text: Passage of the bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act represents one of the most significant federal housing policy achievements in decades—at a time when the nation urgently needs more homes. The enacted legislation brings together a broad set of policies designed to increase housing supply, strengthen affordable housing finance, preserve existing affordable properties, and modernize federal housing programs. Its provisions address nearly every part of the housing ecosystem, from investment capacity and multifamily lending to zoning, permitting, construction methods, and appraisal practices. One of the legislation’s most consequential provisions increases the public welfare investment cap for banks from 15 percent to 20 percent of capital and surplus. The change removes a structural constraint that had begun limiting some banks’ ability to invest in Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) properties and other community development initiatives. The act strengthens affordable housing finance, expands the capacity of private capital, and provides new tools to help communities produce more housing. It is not a stand-alone solution to the housing shortage. Its impact will depend on federal implementation, private-sector investment, and complementary state and local reforms. Still, it provides a clear view of the policy priorities shaping the next phase of federal housing action. Key takeaways The law: Expands banks’ long-term capacity to invest in affordable housing and community development Increases tools to support housing supply through zoning, permitting, planning, and environmental review reforms Updates affordable housing programs, including Rental Assistance Demonstration (RAD), Home Investment Partnerships (HOME), and Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Modernizes financing through small-dollar mortgage initiatives and higher FHA multifamily loan limits Encourages manufactured, modular, and factory-built housing production Includes appraisal and valuation reforms intended to improve confidence in the mortgage process Expanding investment capacity for affordable housing One of the most significant provisions increases the federal public welfare investment cap from 15 percent to 20 percent of a bank’s capital and surplus. Banks use public welfare investments to support affordable housing, community development, and other initiatives that benefit low- and moderate-income communities. These investments include equity investments in properties financed through the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit, the nation’s primary production tool for affordable rental housing. The previous 15 percent cap had increasingly become a constraint for some of the country’s most active affordable housing investors. A 2025 survey of 22 banks by the Affordable Housing Tax Credit Coalition, Affordable Housing Investors Council, and National Assn. of Affordable Housing Lenders, found that participating institutions made approximately $14 billion in housing credit investments in 2024, representing nearly two-thirds of all bank LIHTC investment that year. More than 42 percent of those investments—approximately $6.1 billion—came from banks that were already at or approaching the existing cap. Increasing the cap does not mean banks will immediately increase investment or pay higher prices for housing credits. Investment decisions will continue to reflect Community Reinvestment Act objectives, tax liability, portfolio strategy, market conditions, and risk-adjusted returns. The reform does, however, give banks more room to plan and invest over the long term. Some institutions previously faced a choice between selling existing investments or slowing new investment activity to remain below the regulatory ceiling. Raising the cap allows those banks to manage their portfolios more strategically rather than making decisions primarily to avoid exceeding the limit. The significance of this provision is not that it changes the economics of LIHTC overnight, but it ensures the market has room to grow. Over time, the additional capacity could help create a stronger and more resilient affordable housing finance system, particularly as the supply of housing credits expands and the market seeks additional investor demand. Strengthening affordable housing programs The legislation includes updates to several long-standing affordable housing programs, with a focus on both new production and preservation. Among the most notable provisions is an expansion of the RAD program, increasing its cap from 455,000 to 555,000 units while codifying existing tenant protections. RAD has become one of HUD’s most important preservation tools. It allows public housing agencies to access private financing to rehabilitate aging public housing while maintaining long-term affordability protections. Increasing the cap allows more public housing properties to address deferred maintenance, modernize aging units, and preserve affordable housing for current and future residents. The legislation also reauthorizes and modernizes the HOME Investment Partnerships program, including administrative updates and changes intended to reduce duplicative environmental reviews for certain projects. CDBG programs receive significant attention as well. The legislation adds affordable housing construction as an eligible CDBG activity, giving local governments greater flexibility to use federal resources alongside LIHTC equity, HOME funds, and private investment. It also establishes a pilot program to encourage housing development in participating jurisdictions and provide a multiyear authorization for the Community Development Block Grant–Disaster Recovery program. The added certainty could help states and communities plan for rebuilding housing and infrastructure following federally declared disasters. For multifamily housing, the act also increases Federal Housing Administration (FHA) multifamily loan limits across several programs, reflecting the higher costs of developing and preserving housing in today's market. It also includes updates affecting housing choice vouchers, Family Self-Sufficiency initiatives, and veterans' access to housing programs. Supporting innovation in housing construction The legislation also reflects growing interest in manufactured, modular, prefabricated, and other factory-built construction methods as potential tools for expanding housing supply and controlling costs. It updates the federal definition of manufactured housing to include certain modular and prefabricated homes that are not built on a permanent chassis, while directing HUD to establish appropriate construction and safety standards. Additional provisions require the FHA to evaluate barriers to lending for modular housing, allow HUD to modify financing draw schedules to better support modular construction, modernize manufactured housing lending standards, and reauthorize the Preservation and Reinvestment Initiative for Community Enhancement program to support manufactured housing communities. The changes could help address some of the financing and regulatory barriers facing factory-built housing. However, expanding the sector will also require a deeper and more reliable base of experienced manufacturers. Developers may be hesitant to depend on modular or manufactured construction until there are more financially stable producers capable of delivering large projects consistently. However, policies that make the sector more viable could encourage new participants, strengthen existing manufacturers, and help developers view factory-built housing as a repeatable construction strategy. Looking ahead The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act addresses the nation’s housing challenges from multiple directions—expanding investment capacity, strengthening preservation tools, modernizing financing programs, reducing regulatory barriers, and encouraging new construction methods. Its passage is an important step, but the legislation’s full impact will depend on implementation. Federal agencies must complete rulemaking and establish the processes necessary to put individual provisions into practice. State regulators may need to align their investment rules with new federal limits. Local governments will need to pursue zoning, permitting, infrastructure, and land-use reforms that make additional housing production possible. The legislation also leaves additional work for the housing industry and policymakers. Potential priorities include attracting more investor demand to the LIHTC market, improving the tax treatment of housing credits, addressing bank capital requirements, and ensuring domestic sourcing rules do not unintentionally increase costs or delay affordable housing projects. Still, it signals a meaningful change in the national housing conversation. Affordable housing is increasingly recognized not as an issue limited to specific cities, regions, or political constituencies, but as a challenge affecting communities across the country. For developers, owners, lenders, investors, and public-sector partners, understanding how these provisions interact will be critical to evaluating future financing strategies, development opportunities, and investment decisions. Walker & Dunlop closely monitors legislative and regulatory developments that shape commercial real estate and housing markets. Our professionals help clients understand how changes in federal policies may affect financing strategies, development opportunities, affordable housing initiatives, and long-term investment decisions. Connect with our team to learn more about the potential implications of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act. title: SSC Welcomes Under Armour as Official Conference Apparel Partner
summary: The Sunshine State Conference and Under Armour announce a new five-year agreement, naming Under Armour as the official apparel provider of the 11-team conference beginning July 1, 2026.
body_text: The Sunshine State Conference and Under Armour have announced a new five-year agreement that names Under Armour as the official apparel provider of the 11-team conference beginning July 1, 2026. Founded in 1996, Under Armour has become one of the world’s leading athletic performance brands, known for innovative apparel, footwear, and equipment designed to help athletes perform at their highest level. With a commitment to advancing athletic performance through innovation and technology, Under Armour serves athletes at every level of competition across youth, high school, collegiate, professional, and international sports. The Sunshine State Conference joins the brand’s collegiate roster of more than 300 partnerships. “Under Armour is proud to expand our significant collegiate presence through this new partnership with the Sunshine State Conference.We are excited to support the conference’s tradition of championship-level excellence by outfitting its student-athletes, coaches and institutions with innovative performance products and support that elevates the student-athlete experience.” Craig Cummings Under Armour Vice President, Team Division The Sunshine State Conference, known as the “Conference of National Champions” with 138 national championships across its membership, has established itself as one of Division II’s premier conferences. Committed to championship-level success and the holistic development of student-athletes both athletically and academically, the SSC continues to pursue partnerships that align with those values. As one of the leading brands in collegiate athletics, Under Armour is a natural fit for that mission. “This exciting new venture for the SSC with the leading collegiate sports brand will advance our student-athlete championship experience and overall branding. We are proud to partner with Under Armour to elevate and promote our national championship programs and student-athletes.” Chris Graham SSC Commissioner The agreement represents a shared commitment between the SSC and Under Armour to excellence, innovation, and supporting the continued success of Division II student-athletes.
